reason: The cited evidence (E1) only mentions that Cr coatings peel and crack in high-temperature steam oxidation, but provides no data or discussion on Cr–Zr interdiffusion, TiN as a diffusion barrier, or its deposition and performance. The key premises about the failure mechanism and the proposed solution are entirely unsupported by the provided passage.
premises: Cr coatings on Zr-alloy cladding suffer from Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures, causing premature failure.
TiN has high thermal stability and low diffusivity, making it a suitable diffusion barrier.
A nanoscale TiN interlayer can be deposited between the Zr-alloy substrate and the Cr coating.
The TiN barrier will impede Cr–Zr interdiffusion and prevent formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
This will maintain coating integrity and oxidation resistance under both normal PWR and high-temperature steam conditions.
